title: Invite exemption controls and suspicious-domain workflow for org/team admin flows
creator: Jonah Kim
description:
Background: Current invite pipeline applies a single set of allowlist/denylist checks and domain verification heuristics. Enterprise customers and platform teams have asked for finer-grained admin exemptions and a clearer human review path when a domain is flagged as suspicious. The request must also integrate cleanly with RBAC v2 (so only specific roles can bypass checks), produce immutable audit events, and respect SSO/SAML tenancy policies.

Goal: Implement an invite-exemption + suspicious-domain review workflow that: (1) lets authorized admin roles create scoped exemptions (org or team level) with expiration and justification; (2) surfaces flagged invites in Console with a human-review flow and one-click override (with mandatory reason); (3) emits structured audit logs for every invite decision; (4) ties policy enforcement into RBAC v2 and SSO tenancy (deny bypass if tenant policy forbids); (5) syncs denylist/allowlist signals from external reputation services.

Scope (in-scope): server-side policy engine changes for invite pipeline, DB model for exemptions, Console UI for review + override, audit log schema changes, RBAC v2 checks (role gating), reputation integration (reputation API adapter), feature flag for controlled rollout.

Out of scope: full customer self-service reputation onboarding UI, policy language generalization beyond invites (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Admins with role 'org-security-admin' or 'platform-admin' can create invite exemptions scoped to org or team with optional expiry and free-text justification.
Invite pipeline returns a 'flagged_for_review' status when a domain's reputation score is below threshold and no exemption exists.
Console shows a 'Flagged Invites' queue with invite details, domain reputation score, and a single-click 'Allow with reason' or 'Deny' action. Actions create audit events.

Audit log entry is written for every invite attempt and override containing fields: invite_id, inviter, target_email, domain, reputation_score, policy_decision, acting_admin, justification, timestamp.
RBAC v2 denies the override action when a tenant-level policy explicitly forbids bypass; attempts must surface a clear error to the operator and be logged.
Automated tests cover policy evaluation logic, exemption expiry behavior, and audit log structure; e2e tests exercise the Console review flow and SSO/SSO-tenant denial behavior.
Feature is behind a feature-flag and can be safely rolled back without data loss.
Metrics: flagged_invites_rate, override_rate, time_to_decision (median), and a dashboard for customer impact.
notes: Design trade-offs: store exemptions as first-class DB records vs encode as rules in policy engine. We chose DB records to make auditing and expiry checks simpler and minimize runtime policy language work.
We will gate overrides by RBAC v2 role checks. If RBAC v2 role mapping is missing for an org, default to strict-deny to reduce risk.
Reputation integration: start with a third-party signal provider (fast HTTP adapter) and add caching to avoid throttling. Reputation scores are advisory—policy thresholds determine flagging.
Audit design: logs must be structured JSON shipped to our logging backend with a dedicated index for invite-governance to allow efficient search and retention policies.
Privacy: do not include full invite email local-part in logs for customers who opt-in to strict PII controls; include hashed_email and domain instead.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind 'invite-exemptions' and 'flagged-invite-queue'. Start with internal accounts + 5 customer pilots.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of orgs; monitor override_rate and time_to_decision for 48h.
Phase 2 (expanded): enable for enterprise plan orgs; collect customer feedback and tweak reputation threshold.
If rollback required: flip feature flags off, exemptions remain persisted but ignored by pipeline until safe re-enable.
monitoring: Create dashboard: Invite Governance -> flagged_invites_rate, override_rate, median_time_to_decision, audit_event_count
Alert: override_rate > 2% for 24h OR median_time_to_decision > 4h for 12h
Audit log retention: 365 days for invite governance index (compliance requirement)
Create tracer spans for invite pipeline evaluation to find latency regressions (budget: +20ms p95)
qa_steps: Unit tests for policy matcher, exemptions expiry checks, and RBAC gating logic
Integration tests: reputation API failure mode (timeout/retry) and fallback behavior
E2E test: create invite for flagged domain -> verify Console queue entry -> perform override as authorized admin -> assert audit record and notification to inviter
Security review: run threat model for override flow (malicious admin, audit tampering) and validate immutability of log entries
Performance test: simulate 1000 invites/min pipeline with caching to measure latency impact
